title: Kenyan Seafood Pasta
community: Coastal Kenya — the luxury restaurant pasta
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Seafood Pasta — linguine with Indian Ocean prawns, calamari, and mussels in a white wine, garlic, tomato, and fresh herb sauce. The luxury pasta of Kenya's coastal restaurants — the Indian Ocean's finest in a bowl.
longDesc: Seafood pasta at a Mombasa coastal restaurant is the meeting of Italian pasta technique and Indian Ocean seafood — when the seafood is this fresh and this varied, the dish is extraordinary.
ingredients: ½ cup white wine or fish stock
steps: Cook pasta al dente. Reserve 1 cup pasta water.
In a wide pan, heat olive oil over high heat.
Add calamari rings — cook 2 minutes. Remove.
Add prawns — cook 2 minutes until pink. Remove.
Add mussels and wine. Cover 4—5 minutes until opened.
Add tomatoes and paprika. Cook 4 minutes.
Return all seafood. Add pasta and pasta water.
Add butter. Toss vigorously. Scatter herbs.
chefTips: Seafood timing is critical — calamari and prawns are done in 2 minutes; cook them separately to avoid overcooking.
Discard any mussels that do not open during cooking.
This dish should be assembled and eaten immediately.
commonMistakes: Waiting too long to serve — seafood pasta deteriorates quickly.
cookingScience: See KEN252 for calamari cooking science. In pasta, the calamari should be pulled before fully cooked — it continues cooking in the hot pasta for the final 30 seconds of tossing.
sustainabilityTips: Indian Ocean seafood from coastal Kenyan fishermen — choose sustainably caught species.
culturalNote: Seafood pasta on the Kenyan coast is the happy accident of Italian pasta culture meeting East African fishing traditions — the result is something genuinely world-class when the seafood is as fresh as Kenya's Indian Ocean waters provide.
